topicName: GPT Architecture and Autoregressive Language Modeling

[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"GPT Architecture and Autoregressive Language Modeling"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Generative Pre-trained Transformer (GPT) models have revolutionized Natural Language Processing (NLP) through massive scale and autoregressive training. This tutorial explores the architectural components of GPT and the mechanics of autoregressive language modeling."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding Autoregressive Language Modeling"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Autoregressive modeling generates text sequentially. Given a sequence of tokens, the model predicts the probability distribution of the next token based on all preceding tokens. Mathematically, this is modeled using the chain rule of probability:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"P(w1, w2, ..., wn) = Product from i=1 to n of P(wi | w1, w2, ..., wi-1)"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Unlike masked language models (such as BERT), which look both backward and forward in context, GPT uses causal masking to ensure that a token can only attend to previous tokens in the sequence."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Core Components of the GPT Architecture"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"GPT relies on the decoder-only portion of the original Transformer architecture. Key architectural blocks include:"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Masked Multi-Head Self-Attention: Prevents information leakage from future tokens by applying a lower-triangular mask to the attention matrix."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Position-wise Feed-Forward Networks (FFN): Applied to each position separately and identically, typically consisting of two linear transformations with a non-activation function in between."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Layer Normalization and Residual Connections: Applied either pre-attention/pre-FFN (Pre-LN) or post-attention to stabilize training in deep networks."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Implementing Causal Self-Attention in Python"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Below is a simplified PyTorch implementation demonstrating how the causal mask prevents tokens from attending to future positions:"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class CausalAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, max_len):
        super().__init__()
        self.register_buffer("mask", torch.tril(torch.ones(max_len, max_len)).view(1, 1, max_len, max_len))
    
    def forward(self, q, k, v):
        seq_len = q.size(-2)
        scores = torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-2, -1)) / (q.size(-1) ** 0.5)
        scores.masked_fill_(self.mask[:, :, :seq_len, :seq_len] == 0, float("-inf"))
        attention_weights = torch.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
        return torch.matmul(attention_weights, v)"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Training and Fine-Tuning Dynamics"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"GPT models undergo a two-stage training process:"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Pre-training: The model learns general language representations on massive web-scale corpora using the causal language modeling objective (cross-entropy loss over predicted tokens)."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Fine-Tuning / Alignment: The pre-trained model is adapted to specific downstream tasks or aligned with human preferences via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF)."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"The combination of autoregressive modeling and the scalable decoder-only Transformer architecture forms the foundation of modern Large Language Models (LLMs). Understanding causal masking and next-token prediction is essential for anyone building or researching advanced NLP applications."}]
